newsitem.title: DUBAI: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - Aug 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - Aug 12.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the United Arab Emirates' press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A Dubai official said expatriates with AIDS are immediately deported and blacklisted to prevent their return. He said 179 expatriates were deported for involvement in "immoral" activities and dealing in alcohol in June.
- The UAE's current account surplus is forecast to shrink to 15.4 billion dirhams in 1997 from 23.5 billion dirhams last year, according to the London-based Economist Intelligence Unit.
- The UAE leads other Gulf countries in the battle against film piracy, imposing jail sentences and fines for violators, an official of the Motion Picture Association said.
- Police in the emirate of Ras al Khaimah have lashed several motorists for speeding and other traffic offences.
- The UAE, in an effort to promote tourism, is sprucing up its beaches with facilities to attract a greater number of tourists.

- Abu Dhabi's Saadiyat Free Zone Authority will offer half of its $3.3 billion capital for subscription locally and on international markets. The zone will be built on the island of Saadiyat, east of Abu Dhabi city.
- Sharjah police seized narcotics worth one million dirhams.
- Sales of mobile phones could reach 200 million dirhams by the middle of next year.
- Iraq's Minister of Culture and Information hailed a call by the UAE's president for an Arab summit and the lifting of sanctions on Baghdad.
